title: Making the nitrosonium ion
subtitle: Nitrous acid loses water in acid to give NO⁺

reactants.caption: nitrous acid (from NaNO₂ and HCl) + hydronium ion
reactants.learnerPrompt: Protonate nitrous acid where it will help a leaving group form.
hintTiers: To lose a small stable molecule, nitrous acid needs a good leaving group. Which of its oxygens becomes water if it is protonated?
The OH oxygen uses a lone pair to take a proton from H₃O⁺, and that O–H pair stays on the water oxygen. Two arrows.
Lone pair of the OH oxygen → new bond to a proton of H₃O⁺; that O–H bond → a lone pair on the water oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Protonating the N=O oxygen gives a stabilised cation, but no leaving group: nothing can leave from it. Protonate the OH oxygen, which then leaves as water.
A proton on nitrogen does not create a leaving group. Protonate the OH oxygen.

protonated-acid.caption: protonated nitrous acid + water
protonated-acid.learnerPrompt: Water leaves. Draw how the nitrosonium ion forms.
hintTiers: The N–OH₂⁺ bond can break, taking water away. Which lone pair can make up for the electrons nitrogen loses?
The lone pair of the N=O oxygen forms a second π bond to nitrogen, and the N–O bond to water breaks onto the water oxygen. Two arrows.
N=O oxygen lone pair → another N–O π bond; the bond from nitrogen to the water oxygen → a lone pair on that oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Chloride can displace water to give nitrosyl chloride, ClNO, which is itself a source of NO⁺. The free nitrosonium ion is the electrophile drawn here: let water leave.

steps.explanationAfterStep: Protonating the OH turns it into H₂O⁺, a good leaving group. Nitrous acid is unstable, so it is made in the flask from sodium nitrite and hydrochloric acid at 0–5 °C.

NO⁺, the nitrosonium ion, is isoelectronic with N₂ and CO: N≡O⁺. Its nitrogen is the electrophilic atom that an amine attacks. Breaking only the N–O bond to water is also accepted: N⁺=O, with nitrogen short of an octet, is another drawing of the same ion.

mechanismSummary: Nitrous acid, made in the flask from sodium nitrite and hydrochloric acid, is protonated on its OH group. Water then leaves as the other oxygen's lone pair forms a triple bond to nitrogen, giving the nitrosonium ion, NO⁺: the electrophile that turns an amine into a diazonium ion. Compare the nitronium ion of Electrophilic aromatic substitution.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 23
